THE CHINA PRESS, SUNDAY, DECEMBER 20, 1936
180N-

40 Japanese Executed By "Irregulars"
'Tribune' Correspondent Back In Shanghai From Suiyuan
KEEN INTERVIEWS WANG YING'S MAN
Nipponese Aid To Invaders Confirmed By Newsman

Forty Japanese officers attached to the "Manchukuo"-Mongol "irregulars" were executed near Ulanhua on December 9 by soldiers of a cavalry brigade under the command of bandit chieftain Wang Ying shortly before they surrendered to the Suiyuan Provincial Government troops at Tamiao.

This information, together with other facts which substantiated the belief that Japanese army officers were financing, directing and organizing the "Irregulars'" attack on Suiyuan, was revealed in Shanghai yesterday by Mr. Victor Keen, correspondent of the New York Herald Tribune, who returned Friday from Kweihua, capital of city Suiyuan, where he interviewed General Fu Tso-yi, Provincial Government Chairman, and several army commanders.

12 Days In Kweihua

Mr. Keen left here on December 2, and after spending 12 days in the Suiyuan capital, he proceeded to Pallingmiao, former bandit stronghold which was recently recovered by the Government forces. Although evacuation of all foreigners had been ordered from the area where military operation was in progress by the Government a month ago, Mr. Keen reported that he was given the most courteous treatment by the officers and men under General Fu. He was reminded, however, that he was making the trip at his own risk.

The information of the execution of the 40 Japanese officers, hitherto unknown to the outside world, was obtained by Mr. Keen in an interview with Brigade General Keh Tse-ho, subordinate officer under Wang Ying. General Keh was one of the officers of Wang's cavalry brigade, commanded by General Chin Hsien-chang, which surrendered to the Government at Tamiao, one-time irregular stronghold 80 miles northwest of Pallingmiao.

General Keh in his interview with Mr. Keen declared that Japanese Kwantung Army Headquarters has been financing, directing and organizing the drive on Suiyuan. The military expedition in China's Northwestern province, General Keh told the American correspondent, was directed by a commander-in-chief who was formerly a Colonel of the Kwantung Army. This Nipponese officer, General Keh revealed, is known in his Chinese name as "Hsiao Ping."

This interview, which gives the first authentic information on Japanese participation in the Suiyuan attack, was on December 11 in Kweihua where General Keh had gone to confer with General Fu Tso-yi.

Pressed for further details regarding the role played by the Japanese Kwantung Army officers, General Keh had this to say to Mr.

Paid By Puppets

"All the irregular military units are being paid directly from the Kwantung Army Headquarters at Changchun, capital of the puppet Manchukuo. The Japanese are also supplying military airplanes, pilots, trucks, food and ammunition.

"The irregular army, numbering some 10,000, and commanded by General Li Shoa-hsin participating in the Suiyuan military adventure are entirely directed by Japanese officers.

"When my cavalry brigade surrendered at Tamiao, we turned over 10 field artillery guns, a large number of machine guns, rifles and 150,000 rounds of ammunition. The surrendering unit totaled 1,000 soldiers, forming the 10th cavalry unit of the Mongol forces."

Questioned by Mr. Keen as to the reason for executing the 40 Japanese officers of his brigade, General Keh pointed out that the Nipponese had been arrogant, treating both the Mongols and Chinese as inferiors.

He was then asked by the correspondent whether Colonel Morishima, head of the Japanese military mission at Pailingmiao, prior to its capture by Government forces, was one of the Nipponese army men killed by the soldiers. To this question, General Keh replied:

"I am not sure, but I am told that Colonel Morishima had a beard. Bearded Japanese were among those whom I saw executed near Tamiao."

Apart from the foregoing account he obtained from General Keh, Mr. Keen had obtained the information of the execution of the 40 Japanese from a Government communiqué in Kweihua the previous day.

Japanese In Rear

Continuing with his story of the interview he had with the one-time "irregular" general, Mr. Keen related that he next tried to obtain information on the report that Japanese officers were killed during the Pailingmiao and other Suiquan hostilities.

General Keh said that there is no truth in this report, explaining that the Nipponese were always stationed in the rear when the "Irregulars" attacked. If the operation met with a set-back, General Keh averred, the Japanese officers were previously provided with automobiles to facilitate a hasty escape.

General Keh said that the 40 Nipponese officers attached to his brigade who met their death at the hands of the soldiers included wireless operators and instructors.

The general also revealed that the Japanese officers had supplied his men with poison and smoke screen bombs, but the "irregular" forces refused to use the gas bombs fearing that they would kill large numbers of non-combatants.

Further proof that the Japanese have been supplying the invaders with large amounts of food, munitions and other war materials was obtained by Mr. Keen during his trip to Pailingmiao where he stayed one day. At this city, recently recovered from the "Irregulars," the American correspondent was entertained at breakfast by General Si Lan-feng, commander of the Government troops at Pailingmiao.

Ate Japanese Food

During the meal, Mr. Keen was given Chinese steamed bread made of Japanese flour, and Japanese Toso wine. The breakfast was served on a Japanese-made table. General Siu apologetically explained to the correspondent that the breakfast food was captured from the "Irregulars" when the latter evacuated Pailingmiao.

Pailingmiao and the Government troops garrisoned there appeared to be well-stocked with food, Mr. Keen said. He had been told that for an extended period, General Tso-yi had allowed Japanese trucks from Tientsin, laden with supplies to pass through Kweihua on the way to Pailingmiao. It is believed that a year's supply had been stored in Pailingmiao when the city was attacked and captured by the Government forces.

40名日本人被“非正规军”处决
《论坛报》记者从绥远返回上海
基恩专访王英部属
新闻记者证实日本援助入侵者

12月9日，在土匪头目王英指挥下的一个骑兵旅投降绥远省政府军队于塔庙（Tamiao）之前不久，附属于“满洲国”-蒙古“非正规军”的40名日本军官在乌兰花（Ulanhua）附近被处决。

这一消息，连同其他证实了日本陆军军官正在资助、指挥和组织“非正规军”进攻绥远这一信念的事实，由《纽约先驱论坛报》记者维克多·基恩（Victor Keen）先生昨日在上海披露。基恩先生于周五从绥远省会归化（Kweihua）返回，他在那里采访了省政府主席傅作义将军以及几位军队指挥官。

在归化的12天

基恩先生于12月2日离开此地，在绥远省会度过12天后，他前往百灵庙（Pallingmiao），该地曾是土匪据点，最近被政府军收复。尽管一个月前政府已下令撤离所有正在进行军事行动区域的外国人，但基恩先生报告称，他受到了傅将军麾下官兵最礼遇的对待。不过，他也被告知，此次行程需自负风险。

关于处决40名日本军官的消息，此前外界并不知晓，是基恩先生在采访王英的下属军官葛子浩（Keh Tse-ho，音译）准将时获得的。葛准将是王英骑兵旅的军官之一，该旅由金宪章（Chin Hsien-chang，音译）将军指挥，在塔庙向政府投降，塔庙是位于百灵庙西北80英里处的昔日非正规军据点。

葛将军在接受基恩先生采访时宣称，日本关东军司令部一直在资助、指挥和组织对绥远的进攻。葛将军告诉这位美国记者，在中国西北省份的这次军事远征，是由一位前关东军上校担任总指挥来指挥的。葛将军透露，这名日本军官的中文名字叫“肖平”（Hsiao Ping，音译）。

这次采访提供了关于日本参与进攻绥远的首个真实信息，采访于12月11日在归化进行，当时葛将军前往那里与傅作义将军会商。

当被追问有关日本关东军军官所扮演角色的更多细节时，葛先生对基恩先生说了以下这番话：

由傀儡支付

“所有非正规军事单位的薪饷都直接由伪满洲国首都长春的关东军司令部支付。日本人还提供军用飞机、飞行员、卡车、食物和弹药。

“这支约有1万人的非正规军，由参与绥远军事冒险的李守信（Li Shoa-hsin，音译）将军指挥，完全由日本军官指挥。

“当我的骑兵旅在塔庙投降时，我们移交了10门野战炮、大量机枪、步枪和15万发子弹。投降部队共计1000名士兵，组成了蒙古军队的第10骑兵单位。”

当基恩先生询问处决其旅中40名日本军官的原因时，葛将军指出，日本人一直傲慢无礼，将蒙古人和中国人都视为下等人。

随后，记者问他，在政府军攻占百灵庙之前，担任驻百灵庙日本军事团团长的森岛大佐（Colonel Morishima，音译）是否是被士兵杀死的日本军人之一。对此问题，葛将军回答：

“我不确定，但我听说森岛大佐留有胡须。在我于塔庙附近目睹被处决的人中，有留胡须的日本人。”

除了从葛将军那里获得的上述叙述外，基恩先生还从前一天在归化发布的一份政府公报中获得了处决40名日本人的消息。

日本人在后方

继续讲述他对这位前“非正规军”将军的采访故事，基恩先生叙述道，他接下来试图获取有关在百灵庙及其他绥远战事中日本军官被杀的报告的信息。

葛将军说，这一报告不实，他解释说，当“非正规军”进攻时，日本人总是驻扎在后方。葛将军断言，如果行动受挫，日本军官事先已配备汽车以便迅速逃离。

葛将军说，附属于他的旅并在士兵手中丧生的40名日本军官包括无线电操作员和教官。

这位将军还透露，日本军官曾向其部下提供毒药和烟幕弹，但“非正规”部队拒绝使用毒气弹，因为担心会杀死大量非战斗人员。

基恩先生在前往百灵庙的途中获得了进一步证明日本人一直向入侵者提供大量食物、军火和其他战争物资的证据，他在那里停留了一天。在这座刚从“非正规军”手中收复的城市，美国政府特派记者受到了百灵庙政府军指挥官席兰峰（Si Lan-feng，音译）将军的早餐款待。

食用日本食物

用餐期间，基恩先生享用了用日本面粉制作的中式馒头和日本屠苏酒。早餐是在一张日本制造的桌子上供应的。席将军向记者歉意地解释说，早餐食物是“非正规军”撤离百灵庙时缴获的。

基恩先生说，百灵庙和驻扎在那里的政府部队似乎储备充足。他被告知，在很长一段时间内，傅作义将军允许来自天津、装载物资的日本卡车途经归化前往百灵庙。据信，当政府军攻击并占领该城市时，百灵庙已储存了一年的补给。

National Herald and other local newspapers:

RULES GOVERNING MEDICAL ADVERTISEMENTS

Of late, exaggerated medical advertisements have been appearing in newspapers while certain pages of these newspapers are set aside specially for the publication, under the cloak of propagating common knowledge about medicine and hygiene, of camouflaged medical advertisements.
In view of the above, the Shanghai City Government has instructed the Bureau of Health, the Bureau of Social Affairs and the Bureau of Public Safety to draw up severe measures governing the suppression of such advertisements.
The Bureaux in question have now drafted a set of provisional rules governing the control of medical articles and advertisements of both Chinese and foreign style doctors. It is understood that severe action will be immediately taken to suppress the publication of advertisements that are not in accordance with these rules.

b) 请外交部提出强烈抗议。

December 6, 1936.
Morning Translation.

To Kung Poo and other local newspapers :-

FIGHTING IN SUIYUAN : ACTIVITIES OF LOCAL PUBLIC BODIES

The "Committee to Push Forward the One-Dollar Movement in Aid of Suiyuan" organized by the Shanghai First Special District Citizens' Federation held its first meeting at 2 p.m. yesterday. Some 30 members were present.
The following resolutions were passed :-
1) That Messrs Wong Shiao Lai (王曉籟), Ling Kong Hou (林康侯) and 12 others be appointed standing members of the Committee.
2) That the one-dollar movement be commenced on December 15.
3) That a letter be sent to the Shanghai Second Special District Citizens' Federation and the branches in the Eastern District, the Western District and in Nantao requesting them to start the one-dollar movement at the same time.
4) That all contributions be deposited in the Bank of China.

The General Labour Union, at a meeting held at 2 p.m. yesterday, passed the following resolutions :-
1) That Messrs Tsu Hsueh Van (朱學範) and Chow Hsueh Siang (周孝湘), members of the Union, be appointed representatives to attend the meeting to be held at 10 a.m. December 7 to discuss the calling of a mass meeting.
2) That all labour unions be notified to send representatives to participate in the mass meeting to be held on December 12 by various local public bodies to call attention to the suppression of bandits and the resistance to insults.

In view of the activities of traitors in the rear, the Chinese Seamen's Tangpu will hold a propaganda meeting of seamen at 10 a.m. December 10 at its auditorium to draw the attention of seamen to national salvation work.

Mau Za Chig (毛瑞嘉), Chief of the Yoeh Kwang Nyi Zoen Society (月光藝社), has arranged to give an amusement party in aid of Suiyuan on December 20 in the new building of the Pootung Fellow Provincials Association on Avenue Edward VII.

December 4, 1936. Morning Translation.

China Times and other local newspapers publish the following telegraphic reports :-

THE FIGHTING IN SUIYUAN

Serious fighting has broken out in North Suiyuan. At dawn on December 3, some 5,000 bandits, armed with guns and machine guns and assisted by more than ten aeroplanes, launched an attack on Pailingmiao from the direction of Ta Miao. The attacks were repulsed.. More than 200 bandits were captured. According to the prisoners a certain nation is supplying the bandits with large quantities of firearms, poison gas and aeroplanes. Further attacks by the bandits are expected.
The bandit forces at Nan Hou Chan are being reorganized. A certain nation will supply the bandits with eleven aeroplanes and six tanks. Ten carloads of gasoline were transported from Changteh yesterday. Wong Ying intends to advance to the West by way of North Suiyuan and Wu Chuen.

Local Tangpu to Hold Mass Meeting on December 12

The fighting in Suiyuan Province is becoming more serious daily. The people in the rear should mobilize and render every assistance to the Government.
With a view to reminding the residents in Shanghai of the efforts that are being made to save the nation, the local Tangpu, at a meeting held on December 3, resolved that a mass meeting be convened on December 12, at which attention will be called to the suppression of bandits, the extermination of traitors, resistance to insults and the salvation of the nation. It was also resolved that a procession be held at Nantao on that day and lectures be given on the route of the procession.
It further resolved that all local broadcasting stations be notified to broadcast addresses to remind the people of the national crisis.
Mr. Loh Ching Sz (陸京士) of the local Tangpu has been assigned the task of making arrangements for the time and the venue of the proposed mass meeting.

The Ba Chen (培成) Middle School for Girls, Ferry Road, has solicited contributions amounting to $5,476.60. The teachers and the students are making 2,000 padded cotton vests to be sent to the officers and men engaged in the bandit suppression campaign in Suiyuan. Medicines for the soldiers have also been procured.
Mr. Zau Vee Feng (曹未風), a representative of the school, will leave for Suiyuan to-day to console the soldiers at the front.

The Ba Min (培明) Middle School for Girls, Hart Road, has collected a sum of $987. The money is being used for the purchase of padded cotton clothing for the manufacture of 1,000 vests. The clothing is being made by the students themselves.

绥远战事

绥远北部爆发激烈战斗。12月3日黎明，约5000名配备枪支和机枪并在十余架飞机协助下的匪徒，从大庙方向向百灵庙发动攻击。攻击被击退。俘虏匪徒200余名。据俘虏称，某国正向匪徒提供大量枪械、毒气和飞机。预计匪徒将进一步发动攻击。
南壕堑的匪军正在重组。某国将向匪徒提供11架飞机和6辆坦克。昨日从常德运出十车汽油。王英意图经由绥北和五原向西推进。

当地党部将于12月12日举行群众大会

绥远省战事日益严峻。后方民众应动员起来，全力协助政府。
为提醒上海居民关注救国努力，当地党部于12月3日召开会议，决议于12月12日召开群众大会，呼吁关注剿匪、肃清汉奸、抵抗侮辱及拯救国家。还决议当日在南市举行游行，并在游行路线上进行演讲。
会议还决议通知本地所有广播电台广播演讲，提醒民众注意国家危机。
当地党部的陆京士（Loh Ching Sz）先生已被指派负责安排拟议中群众大会的时间和地点。

渡轮路培成女中已募集捐款5,476.60元。师生正在制作2,000件棉背心，送往绥远剿匪前线的官兵。还采购了士兵用药。
该校代表曹未风（Zau Vee Feng）先生将于今日前往绥远慰问前线士兵。

哈特路培明女中已筹集款项987元。该款项用于购买棉花制作1,000件背心。衣物由学生亲自制作。

JAPANESE MARINES LANDED AT TSINGTAO

In the small hours of the morning of
December 3, seven Japanese warships arrived at Tsingtao.
At 4 a.m. more than 500 Japanese marines were landed
and proceeded to the Tangpu, the City Government Library,
the National Athletics Training Association, the Kioochow-
Tsinan Railway Tangpu and the "Ping Min Pao" newspaper
office, where, after conducting a search, they took away
a number of official documents and arrested nine persons.
As a result of a protest by the Tsingtao City Government,
the arrested persons were released at 11 a.m.
The Japanese marines are being concentrated in
the vicinity of the various Japanese cotton mills at
Chonkow (滄口) and Szefang (四方). The Japanese
authorities are using the strike of workers in Japanese
cotton mills in Tsingtao as a pretext to despatch landing
forces to Tsingtao for the ostensible purpose of according
protection to Japanese residents. Mayor Sung Hung Lih
(沈鴻烈) of the Tsingtao City Government has lodged a
protest with the Japanese authorities.
It is learned that during their search at
the above mentioned places, the marines cut off the
telephone lines, while some of the arrested persons were
assaulted and injured.

Date 3 / 12 / 36

December 3, 1936. Afternoon Translation.

Lih Pao publishes the following article contributed by one
Chen Chih :-

STREET COLLECTIONS BY STUDENTS

The following statement was made to me by one
of the students who participated in the movement to solicit
public contributions on the streets in aid of the officers
and men fighting at the front in Suiyuan:-

"Most of the contributions come from the poor.
The persons who belong to the motor car class regard us,
students, as a nuisance. Whenever they see us approaching
their charffeurs would be instructed to put on speed.
Then the Police came and seized all our banners and
contribution boxes and took us to the Police Station where
we were severly reprimanded for disturbing the peace and
order and were warned against further soliciting for
contributions on the streets. All these words and
admonition sounded like thunder to me and I began to
wonder to whom this territory belong, from whom and for
whom these contributions were being collected".

《立报》刊登陈智撰写的以下文章：-

学生街头募捐

一位参与为绥远前线作战官兵募集公众捐款的学生向我作了如下陈述：-

“大部分捐款来自穷人。属于汽车阶层的人视我们学生为麻烦。每当他们看到我们走近，就会吩咐司机加速离开。随后警察前来，没收了我们所有的旗帜和捐款箱，并将我们带到警察局，在那里我们因扰乱治安秩序受到严厉斥责，并被警告不得再在街头募捐。这些言语和训诫对我而言如雷贯耳，我开始疑惑这片土地究竟属于谁，这些捐款是向谁募集、又是为了谁。”

Sin Wan Pao and other local newspapers:

THE NAKAYAMA MURDER CASE

The appeal of Yang Wen Dao (楊文道) and
Yih Hai Sung (叶海生) against the sentence of death
passed on them by the First Shanghai Special District Court
for the murder of the Japanese marine named Nakayama was
to have been heard by the Second Branch of the Kiangsu
High Court on November 20, but owing to the sickness of
Yang Wen Dao, the hearing was postponed to the morning of
December 2.
It is learned that as Yang is still ill,
the hearing of the appeal to-day may again be postponed.

Min Pao and other local newspapers:

CONTRIBUTIONS TO DEFENCE FORCES IN SUIYUAN

With a view to accelerating the "one-day"
movement, the various local seamen's bodies held a joint
meeting at 3 p.m. yesterday at which it was resolved that
an Acceleration Committee of Chinese Seamen to Contribute
One Day's Pay be established at the office of the Seamen's
Tangpu. This Committee will have three members.

In compliance with the request of the Red
Cross Service Committee, the Shanghai Native Bankers
Guild has decided that every member of the Guild should
contribute $100 in aid of the officers and men fighting
at the front.

The employees of the Chinese Merchants
Steam Navigation Company and the Tai Kong Biscuits and
Canned Provisions Company are raising contributions of
one day's pay in aid of the men in Suiyuan.

The Ningpo Fellow Provincials Association
will notify all its fellow provincials to raise contributions.
Yesterday the Chinese Cotton Exchange
Brokers Association contributed $9,000 through the Chung
Wei Bank for remittance to the Suiyuan authorities. It is
learned that the Association will raise another $2,000
in the next few days.

The local Women's Committee to Solicit
Contributions has made arrangements with the Shanghai Radio
Broadcasting Station of the Ministry of Communications for
the broadcasting of propaganda urging women to contribute
fur waist-coats, gloves, etc.

At 3 p.m. yesterday, the Committee to
accelerate One Day's Pay Contribution Movement held a
meeting at its office on Rue Lafayette, French Concession,
at which were present representatives from the Shanghai
Special District Kuomintang Headquarters, the Shanghai
City Government, the Woosung-Shanghai Garrison Commissioner's
Headquarters, the Bureaux of Social Affairs and Education,
the General Labour Union, the Shanghai Peasants' Association,
the Shanghai District Association, the Newspaper Reporters
Association, the Shanghai Bar Association, the Shanghai
Medical Practitioners Association and the Shanghai Citizens
Federations of the International Settlement and the French
Concession. Mr. Tung Ying Bah (董行白) of the local
Tangpu presided.

《新闻报》及其他本地报纸：-

中山谋杀案

杨文道和叶海生因谋杀日本海军陆战队士兵中山而被上海第一特区地方法院判处死刑，二人提出上诉。该上诉原定由江苏高等法院第二分院于11月20日审理，但因杨文道生病，听证会推迟至12月2日上午。
据悉，由于杨氏仍在病中，今天的上诉听证可能会再次推迟。

《民报》及其他本地报纸：-

向绥远国防部队捐款

为加速“一日捐”运动，本地各海员团体于昨日下午3时举行联席会议，决议在海员工部办事处成立“中国海员一日薪捐献加速委员会”。该委员会将由三名成员组成。

应红十字会服务委员会的请求，上海钱业公会决定，公会每位会员捐款100元，以援助前线作战官兵。

招商局和泰康饼干罐头食品公司的员工正在募集一日薪金，以援助绥远将士。

宁波同乡会将通知所有同乡进行捐款。
昨日，华商纱布交易所经纪人协会通过中汇银行捐款9,000元，汇往绥远当局。据悉，该协会将在未来几天内再筹集2,000元。

本地妇女募捐委员会已与交通部上海广播电台达成协议，广播宣传呼吁妇女捐赠皮背心、手套等物品。

昨日下午3时，“加速一日薪捐献运动委员会”在法租界霞飞路的办事处举行会议，出席者包括国民党上海特别市党部、上海市政府、吴淞上海警备司令部、社会局和教育局、总工会、上海农民协会、上海区协会、新闻记者公会、上海律师公会、上海医师公会以及公共租界和法租界的上海市民联合会代表。会议由本地党部的董行白先生主持。

December 1, 1936.
Morning Translation

Sin Wan Pao and other local newspapers publish the following telegraphic reports :-

THE SITUATION IN SUIYUAN

At a military conference held in the Chia Po Sz Temple by Muto, Chief of the Second Section of the Kwantung Army, and Senior Staff Officer Yoshioka of the 7th Division in Jehol, it was decided that the bandit and "Menchukuo" forces under Wong Ying and Lee Shou Shing be ordered to be on the defensive with Shangtu as their base, while the reinforcements from Jehol under Pao Yoh Ching are to launch an attack on Pailingmiao. The strength of each unit is estimated at 20,000 men, with aeroplanes and armoured cars.

General Yen Hsi Shan has raised a loan of $2,210,000 to meet the expenses for the bandit suppression campaign.

As funds are badly needed for the suppression of bandits in Shansi and Suiyuan, the Ministry of Finance has remitted $500,000 to Suiyuan. The Ministry has also approved the request of the Shansi Provincial Government for permission to issue debenture bonds to the amount of $10,000,000. The request will be referred to the Executive Yuan for approval.

Sin Wan Pao and other local newspapers :-

Mr. Lee Hung Wen(李鴻文), a delegate of General Yen Hsi Shan, arrived in Shanghai from Nanking by rail yesterday morning. At 11 a.m. Mr. Lee called on Dr. H.H. Kung at the Central Bank of China, to whom he made a report on the situation in Shansi and Suiyuan and requested financial assistance. At 4 p.m. Mr. Lee, accompanied by Mr. Yen Tsu Yuen(閻敘遠), a former General in the Shansi Army, paid a visit to Mr. Ling Kong Hou(林康侯) at the Bankers Association, after which the callers proceeded to the Chinese Chamber of Commerce where they met Messrs. Wong Shiao Lai, Tu Yuet Sen, Yen Foh Ching, Loh Ching Sz, Huang Yee Zei and Baung Ching Chow, to whom Mr. Lee expressed the appreciation of General Yen Hsi Shan. Discussion was then held regarding the appropriation of public contributions and the procuring of gas masks.
It is understood that Mr. Lee will remain here for one or two more days.

"Association of Benevolent Bodies in Shanghai to Afford Relief to Refugees and Wounded Soldiers in Bandit Devastated Areas in Suiyuan"

At 4 p.m. yesterday, various benevolent bodies in Shanghai inaugurated an "Association of Benevolent Bodies in Shanghai to Afford Relief to Refugees and Wounded Soldiers in Bandit Devastated Areas in Suiyuan Province" at the Jen Chi Daung (仁濟堂) Benevolent Institution, Yunnan Road. Some 200 persons including Messrs Tu Yuet Sen (杜月笙), Wong Shiao Lai (王曉), Wong Yih Ding (王一亭) and Choeh Wen Loh (陸文六) and representatives of the China

《新闻报》及其他本地报纸刊登下列电讯报道：

绥远局势

在察哈尔省多伦诺尔（Chia Po Sz Temple，音译）寺庙举行的军事会议上，关东军第二课课长武藤（Muto）与驻热河第七师团高级参谋吉冈（Yoshioka）决定，命令王英和李守信率领的匪帮及“满洲国”部队以商都（Shangtu）为基地采取守势，而由鲍玉清（Pao Yoh Ching，音译）率领的热河援军则进攻百灵庙。估计各部兵力约为两万人，配有飞机和装甲车。

阎锡山将军已筹集贷款2,210,000元，以支付剿匪战役的费用。

由于山西和绥远剿匪急需资金，财政部已向绥远汇去500,000元。财政部还批准了山西省政府关于发行10,000,000元公债的请求。该请求将提交行政院核准。

《新闻报》及其他本地报纸：

阎锡山将军的代表李鸿文先生昨晨乘火车从南京抵达上海。上午11时，李先生在中国银行拜访孔祥熙博士，向其汇报山西和绥远的局势，并请求财政援助。下午4时，李先生在前晋军将领阎叙远先生的陪同下，前往银行公会拜访林康侯先生，随后访客们前往上海总商会，会见了王晓籁、杜月笙、严佛清、罗敬思、黄奕赓和邦庆周（Baung Ching Chow，音译）等先生，李先生向他们转达了阎锡山将军的谢意。随后就公共捐款的拨付及防毒面具的采购事宜进行了讨论。
据悉，李先生将在此停留一两天。

“上海慈善团体联合救济绥远匪患区难民伤兵协会”

昨日下午4时，上海各慈善团体在云南路仁济堂慈善机构发起成立“上海慈善团体联合救济绥远省匪患区难民伤兵协会”。约200人出席，包括杜月笙、王晓（Wong Shiao Lai，原文如此，通常为王晓籁）、王一亭、陆文六（Choeh Wen Loh，音译）等先生以及中国

December 1, 1936. Morning Translation.

Red Cross Society, the Shanghai Orphans Institute, the Chinese Women and Children Relief Association, the China Leper Relief Association etc. were present.
Mr. Choeh Wen Loh, who presided, made the following report:- "Fighting has broken out in Suiyuan. Numerous wounded soldiers and refugees in the war devastated areas have become homeless and many have lost their lives. For this reason, this new Association is being formed for the purpose of affording them relief. The Famine Relief Committee has promised to issue bonds to the value of $100,000 to assist the Association."
Dr. H.H. Kung, Minister of Finance, was appointed Chairman of the new Association with the following gentlemen as Vice Chairmen: Mayor Wu Te Chen, Dr. C.T. Wang, Messrs Fan Kung Chan, Tu Yuet Sen, Wong Yih Ding, Tsu Ts Jao (朱子橋), Yih Tso Chong (叶楚傖), Choeh Wen Loh and Hsiung Hsi Ling (熊希齡).

First Special District Citizens Federation To Hold Meeting

On November 30, the First Special District Citizens Federation sent copies of the following letter to the representatives of its branches :-
"In view of the gravity of the situation in Suiyuan, this Federation has initiated a 'one-dollar movement in aid of Suiyuan'. The Federation will hold a meeting at 2 p.m. December 2 to discuss measures to enforce this movement. You are requested to attend the meeting."

Performance for Benefit of Suiyuan Forces.

(兒童劇社) The other day the "Er Dong Dramatic Society" suggested that local dramatic societies stage a performance for the benefit of the Government forces in Suiyuan.
The "Sz Zuh Nyi Dai"(四十年代), the "Hai Yien"(海燕), the "Da Hsia"(大夏), the "Tsung Foong"(春風), the "Liang Tsai"(量才) and the "Nan Sang"(南僑) Dramatic Societies have expressed their willingness to participate in this performance. Representatives of these dramatic societies will hold a meeting at 5 p.m. December 3 at the Victoria Theatre, Haining Road, to discuss preparations for the performance.

National Herald :-

THE REPORT OF THE STAFF ECONOMY COMMITTEE.

A committee has been formed by the Chinese Staff Association of the Shanghai Municipal Council to study those points in the report of the Staff Economy Committee which are considered prejudicial to the interests of the Chinese staff. The Association will probably oppose the recommendations of the Staff Economy Committee.

为绥远部队筹款的义演。

“四十年代”、“海燕”、“大夏”、“春风”、“量才”和“南侨”剧社已表示愿意参加此次义演。这些剧社的代表将于12月3日下午5时在海宁路维多利亚剧院举行会议，讨论演出筹备工作。

What is Miss Sze Liang afraid of? If she
is truly patriotic, she should be ready for any sacrifice.
In our opinion, there is no possibility of any of the

and 39 others as members.

Propaganda by Broadcasting

绥远部队捐款

通过以下决议：
1) 以会议名义发表宣言。
2) 以会议名义发出慰问绥远剿匪官兵的电报。
3) 成立“上海各界募集防毒面具援助绥远军队委员会”，成员包括俞亚青、方椒伯、顾馨一、诸文绮等39人。

广播宣传

鉴于绥远发生战事，所有中国人都有义务为国效力，隐隐歌咏团已在全市合唱界发起运动，通过广播电台劝说公众捐款援助前线官兵。凡愿意参加广播的各团体和公共组织，请于12月1日至5日期间致函南京路沙逊大厦交通部广播电台申请。

November 26, 1936. Morning Translation.

Sin Wan Pao and other local newspapers publish the following telegraphic reports :-

THE SITUATION IN SUIYUAN

A certain nation has supplied the insurgents under Lee Chou Shing with 20 aeroplanes and 30 tanks. A big offensive will be launched against the Government positions at Tacling and Shingwc as soon as the concentration of bandit and "Manchukuo" forces has been completed. Reinforcements for the bandit forces are now pouring into Saungtu.

The "Manchukuo" and Mongolian forces at Saungtu are organizing a Dare-To-Die Corps which will be directed by the people of a certain nation in an attack on Pailingmiao. The formation of a Chemical Fighting Unit is also in progress. Poison gases will be used.

On November 27, several aeroplanes belonging to a certain nation flew over Pailingmiao and dropped several bombs.

Lih Pao and other local newspapers :-

Activities of Local Public Bodies.

The "Committee to Send Consolation and Aid to the Officers and Men engaged in Bandit Suppression in Suiyuan Province" held a meeting at 4 p.m. yesterday. Mr. Doo Yuet Sen presided.

Mr. Wong Shao Lai and other delegates of the Committee who went recently to Suiyuan to console the Government troops submitted to the meeting a written report which read, in part, as follows :-

"We arrived at Taiyuan at 10 a.m. November 24 and on the following day we flew to Suiyuan. We had an interview with General Fu Tso Nyi who expressed thanks on behalf of his men for the donation of a sum of $100,000 contributed by the public in Shanghai. General Fu informed us that when he captured Pailingmiao, they seized large quantities of munitions, petrol and 20,000 bags of flour. A number of people closely resembling the subjects of a certain nation were discovered among the prisoners. They refused to speak. In all, four aeroplanes have been shot down by the Government troops. On the morning of November 26 we flew to Loyang where we interviewed General Chiang Kai Shek who declared that he had already resolved to suppress the bandits in Suiyuan."

At 5 p.m. yesterday the Committee to Support the Bandit Suppression in Suiyuan organized by local Chinese cultural circles held a meeting in the office of the Chinese Cultural Promotion Association.

The following resolutions were passed :-
(1) That a telegram be sent requesting General Sung Cheh Yuan to instruct the Charhar Authorities to despatch troops to assist in the suppression of the Mongolian, "Manchukuo" and bandit forces in North Charhar.

《新闻报》及其他本地报纸刊登下列电讯报道：

绥远局势

某国已向李守信率领的叛军提供20架飞机和30辆坦克。一旦匪帮和“满洲国”部队集结完毕，将对大清（Tacling，音译）和兴和（Shingwc，音译）的政府阵地发动大规模进攻。匪帮援军正源源不断涌入商都（Saungtu，音译）。

商都的“满洲国”和蒙古部队正在组织敢死队，将由某国人士指挥进攻百灵庙。化学作战部队也在组建中。将使用毒气。

11月27日，几架属于某国的飞机飞越百灵庙上空，投下数枚炸弹。

《立报》及其他本地报纸：

本地公共团体的活动。

“慰问绥远省剿匪官兵委员会”于昨日下午4时举行会议。杜月笙先生主持。

委员会近期赴绥远慰问政府军的代表王晓籁先生等人向会议提交了一份书面报告，部分内容如下：

“我们于11月24日上午10时抵达太原，次日飞往绥远。我们会见了傅作义将军，他代表部下感谢上海公众捐赠的100,000元款项。傅将军告知我们，攻克百灵庙时，缴获了大量弹药、汽油和20,000袋面粉。在俘虏中发现数名外貌酷似某国臣民的人。他们拒绝说话。政府军共击落四架飞机。11月26日上午，我们飞往洛阳，会见了蒋介石将军，他表示已决心肃清绥远匪患。”

昨日下午5时，由本地中国文化界组织的“支援绥远剿匪委员会”在中国文化促进会办公室举行会议。

通过以下决议：
(1) 发电报请求宋哲元将军指示察哈尔当局派兵协助肃清察哈尔北部的蒙古、“满洲国”及匪帮部队。

Min Pao and other local newspapers :-

THE KAYAU MURDER CASE.

In connection with the murder of Mr. Kayau,
a Japanese resident, the Bureau of Public Safety sometime
ago arrested Wong Tseng Sung (王振声), Mau Yung Fu (毛永甫),
Kyung Tao Hwang (金道横) and three others and charged them
before the Shanghai District Court at Nantao.
It is learned that the case will be given a
further hearing to-day before the Presiding Judge Tsai Ting
Zung (蔡鼎成) and Judges Li Yok Tung (李育燈) and Chac Tsen
Jih (查森植) at the Shanghai District Court. Nine Japanese
witnesses have been summoned to give evidence.

加藤谋杀案。

就日侨加藤先生（Mr. Kayau）被杀一案，公安局日前逮捕了王振声、毛永甫、金道横（音译）等三人及其他人员，并向南市上海地方法院提起公诉。

November 27, 1936.
Afternoon Translation.

Activities of Local Public Bodies

Acting on a resolution passed by a meeting
held recently, the Shanghai First Special District Citizens'
Federation on November 26 sent a letter to the local
"Committee to Send Consolation and Aid to the Officers and
Men engaged in Bandit Suppression in Suiyuan Province",
requesting it to initiate a big campaign for the collection
of contributions to purchase anti-gas masks.

At 6 p.m. yesterday, the North-West Question
Research Committee held a meeting at the Chinese Y.M.C.A.,
Boulevard de Montigny, French Concession, Mr. Li Dah Chao
(李大超) presided. The following resolutions were passed:-
1) That a telegram be dispatched to General Sung Cheh Yuan
of Peiping urging him to mobilize his troops to assist
in the suppression of bandits in Suiyuan.
2) That a circular addressed to the people in the North-
West be issued.

On November 26, the Drivers' Mutual Aid
Association of the China General Omnibus Company announced
that members of the Association will contribute one-day's
wages towards the fund in aid of the officers and men at
the front in Suiyuan.

The pupils of the Wu Lun (扶轮) Primary
School at Woosung, established by the Ministry of Railways,
are collecting contributions from passengers on the trains
running between Shanghai and Woosung.

The Lih Tuh (立德) Primary School, Connaught
Road, held a meeting yesterday and passed the following
resolutions :-
1) That the teachers and pupils of the school fast for
one day and contribute the money saved in aid of the
officers and men at the front in Suiyuan.
2) That teachers contribute 10 per cent of their wages.

November 27, 1936.    2    Morning Translation.

Shun Pao and other local newspapers :-

CONTRIBUTIONS TO DEFENDERS OF SUIYUAN

According to the Ta Kung News Agency,
the local General Labour Union, with a view to rising
contributions in aid of the bandit suppression forces in
Suiyuan, will, on November 27, conduct an extensive
propaganda amongst labourers to contribute one day's pay.
The following methods will be adopted:-
(1) Propaganda groups will be organized among the members
and labour trainers of the General Labour Union, the
China Labour Federation and the Yung Tsin Society
(勇進社) to conduct propaganda among the various
factories. One member of the group will be assigned
to each factory.
(2) The members of the propaganda groups will be provided
with forms which are to be filled in by them after
they have completed their work.
(3) Each member of the propaganda group will be provided
with a written outline of subjects to be used in the
propaganda work.
(4) Members of the propaganda groups will be provided
with copies of propaganda literature to be distributed
among the workers of the factory.
(5) Arrangements will be made for the loan of two radio
broadcasting stations and Messrs. Chu Yoh Wei (朱學範)
and Chow Yoh Hsiang (周孝湘), members of the General
Labour Union, will be invited to broadcast addresses.
(6) The propaganda will not be conducted in the factories
and labour unions which have already started such
a movement.
(7) News items relating to this movement are to be issued
on November 26.
The members of the propaganda groups
will operate among the factories located in the following
districts:-
Tung Ka Doo, Hu Ka Lou Jao, Nyi Ziang
Chuan, Lai Nee Doo, Loh Ka Tse, Sin Mou Road, Kao Jao and
Tung Cheu in Pootung; Loh Ka Pang, Hai Zau Shih Temple,
Kuo Fu Road, Kao Chong Miao and Jih Huei Kong in Natao;
Paoshan Road, Tien-Tung-An Station, Wang Pang Road, Chungshan
Road, Ta Tung Road, Kung Woo Road, Hung Feng Road, Chung Hing
Road, Tan Tse Wei, And Hai Chong Road in Chapei; Zau Ka Doo;
Robison Road; Tonguin Road, Kiangwan; Woosung; Kao Loong
Jao; Yangtszepoo; Ying Ziang Kong; Siccawei; Lunghwa; and
Fah-Hwa Village.
It is learned that Messrs. Chu Yoh Wei
and Chow Yoh Hsiang, members of the Standing Committee of
the General Labour Union, will deliver addresses through
the Radio Broadcasting Station (K.C. 1,300) in the Sassonn
House. Mr. Chu will speak from 9.30 to 9.50 p.m. to-day,
while Mr. Chow will speak from 9.50 to 10.10 p.m. to-day.

Local Delegates Return from Suiyuan

Messrs. Wong Shao Iai (王曉籟); Ling Kong
Hou (林康侯) and other delegates who left for Suiyuan on
November 23 to console the bandit suppression officers and
men at the front returned to Shanghai yesterday afternoon.
In a Press interview, one of the delegates
made the following statement:- "The fighting spirit of the
officers and men at the front is very high. The bandits
have been completely driven out of Suiyuan territory.
Evidence has been secured proving that a certain nation is
aiding the bandits and will be used in future negotiations."

1936年11月27日。    2    晨间译件。

《申报》及其他本地报纸：

捐助绥远守军

据大公通讯社报道，本地总工会为筹集款项援助绥远剿匪部队，将于11月27日在劳工中开展广泛宣传，号召捐献一日工资。
将采取以下方法：
(1) 在总工会、中国劳动协会及勇进社的会员和劳工训练员中组织宣传队，在各工厂进行宣传。每个工厂指派一名宣传队员。
(2) 向宣传队员提供表格，由其在工作完成后填写。
(3) 向每位宣传队员提供用于宣传工作的书面提纲。
(4) 向宣传队员提供宣传刊物副本，以便在工厂工人中分发。
(5) 安排借用两个广播电台，并邀请总工会成员朱學範先生和周孝湘（音译）先生发表广播讲话。
(6) 已在开展此类运动的工厂和工会不进行此项宣传。
(7) 有关此次运动的新闻稿将于11月26日发布。
宣传队员将在以下地区的工厂开展工作：
浦东的唐家渡、胡家楼角、倪家船、赖泥渡、罗家宅、新茂路、高桥和东沟；南市的罗家浜、海潮寺、国富路、高昌庙和日晖港；闸北的宝山路、天通庵站、王浜路、中山路、大通路、公兴路、鸿丰路、中兴路、潭子湾和海昌路；曹家渡；罗宾森路（Robison Road）；同文路（Tonguin Road）、江湾；吴淞；高隆桥（音译）；杨树浦；引翔港（音译）；徐家汇；龙华；以及法华村。
据悉，总工会常务委员朱學範先生和周孝湘（音译）先生将通过萨逊大厦（Sassoon House）的广播电台（K.C. 1,300）发表讲话。朱先生将于今晚9:30至9:50讲话，周先生将于今晚9:50至10:10讲话。

本地代表从绥远返回

王晓籁、林康侯等代表于11月23日启程前往绥远慰劳前线剿匪将士，于昨日下午返回上海。
其中一位代表在接受记者采访时发表如下声明：“前线将士战斗精神高昂。匪徒已被彻底逐出绥远境内。已获取证据证明某国正在援助匪徒，这些证据将在未来的谈判中使用。”

At a weekly memorial service held by the
Shih Chung Middle School for Girls ( 治中女中 ), Nanyang
Road, yesterday morning, Miss Chen Nai Wen ( 陳乃文 ),
the principal, made a report on the movement among the
schools to raise contributions towards the support of
the troops in Suiyuan.
Moved by the report, some 20 students set
out in the afternoon to solicit contributions from the
public. At 5.30 p.m. two girl students were arrested
and taken by foreign policemen to Sinza Station as
they were raising contributions from pedestrians on the
pavement on the east side of the Park Hotel on Bubbling
Well Road.
Upon receipt of this information, Mr. Chang
Chung Yin ( 張仲揆 ), Chairman of the Board of Directors
of the school, immediately called at Sinza Station in
person and opened negotiations, as a result of which the
two girls were released shortly after 6 p.m. It is
reported that a sum of $20 was raised by them yesterday.

The Holmes :-

THE REGISTRATION OF CULTURAL BODIES

According to the rules laid down by the National Government, a cultural body must apply for registration with the authorities of the district wherein it is located; it must also register with the Tangpu. Failure to do this would render it liable to suppression.
Shanghai has more cultural bodies that any other city in China. Many of them are properly registered but a large number are still unregistered.
The other day, Mr. Pan Kung Chai, Commissioner of the Bureau of Social Affairs, summoned the members of the Shanghai Special District Kuomintang Headquarters to a meeting to discuss this matter.
It was resolved that from November 21 until the end of this year, all local cultural bodies are to be ordered to apply for registration with the local authorities and the Tangpus. Mr. Pan Kung Chai will attend to the Bureau of Social Affairs, while Mr. Tao Pah Chuen will officiate for the Tangpu.
It is reported that since the promulgation of these measures, a large number of cultural bodies have applied to the authorities for registration.

文化团体的注册

根据国民政府的规定，文化团体必须向其所在地区的当局申请注册；还必须在党部注册。未能这样做将使其面临被取缔的风险。

November 25, 1936. Afternoon Translation.

The Committee to support Suiyuan organized by
Chinese cultural circles in this locality has drawn up
the following measures for the collection of contributions:-
1) Every unit is to undertake the collection of contributions;
the money is to be deposited in a bank.
2) An individual who has collected contributions must hand
the money over to the organization with which he is
connected. The money will afterwards be sent to a bank.
3) The Committee will form contributions soliciting sections.

Local fellow provincials associations used to
hold a dinner party once every month. In view of the
invasion of Suiyuan by the bandits, these associations
held a meeting at 8 p.m. yesterday at the Dong Shing Leu
Restaurant (同兴楼), Foochow Road, and discussed the
raising of contributions.
It was decided to save a part of the money for
the dinner and to send the money to the fund in aid of the
officers and men at the front.

The students of the Shih Chung Middle School
for Girls (市女中), Nanyang Road, are continuing to collect
contributions for the support of the officers and men at
the front in Suiyuan despite the fact that two days ago
two of the girl students were arrested. On November 24,
some 60 students were engaged in this work; a few solicited
contributions on the streets, but the majority approached
relatives and friends. They collected about $180.
The school authorities yesterday made an
explanation to the S.M.C. about the collection, therefore
nothing untoward occurred.
The school will close on Friday to enable
students to make cotton clothing to be sent to the front.

At 2 p.m. yesterday, the local Middle School
Teachers' Federation held a meeting with the principals
of middle schools at the Dah Sie Yang Restaurant (大西洋).
It was resolved that all schools refrain from
soliciting contributions from the general public.

Yesterday, the "Ta Kung Pao" received the
following contributions :-
1) Teaching staff, students and coolies of the Great China
University - $1,080.
2) Employees of the China Cotton Trading Company - $256.50.
3) Shanghai Office of the Szechuen Commercial Bank - $100.
4) Employees of the Ta Dong Shipping Company - $429.
5) Employees of the Foh Hsin Rolled Tobacco Factory -
$612.61.
6) Officers of various official organs in Yen Chen Hsien,
Shantung Province - $128.50.

本地各同乡会以往每月举行一次聚餐。鉴于匪徒进犯绥远，这些同乡会于昨晚8时在福州路同兴楼餐厅举行会议，讨论募集捐款事宜。

November 25, 1936. Morning Translation

Ta Kung Pao and other local newspapers publish the following telegraphic reports :-

THE SITUATION IN SUIYUAN : CHINESE GOVERNMENT TROOPS OCCUPY PAILINGMIAO.

The Chinese Government troops occupied Pailingmiao at 9.30 a.m. November 24.

Acting on information that reinforcements of about 5000 Mongolian and Manchukuo soldiers were due to arrive at Pailingmiao on the afternoon of November 24, the Government troops under the command of General Tseng Yen Shou (曾延授) launched a general offensive against Pailingmiao at 1 a.m. November 24 from Wuchuen and Kooyang. The Mongolian and Manchukuo forces were directed by 200 military officers of a certain nation. A fierce battle ensued, which resulted in the occupation of Pailingmiao at 9.30 a.m. by the Government forces. The latter lost 300 dead and wounded, whilst the enemy forces were annihilated. The Chinese cavalry are pursuing the fleeing Mongolian and Manchukuo troops and the people of a certain nation.

As Prince Teh is eager to surrender to the Chinese Government, a certain nation has appointed Tanaka, Chief of the Special Military Organ, to keep a close watch on the movements of Prince Teh.

On November 24, high military officers of the Japanese forces stationed in North China held a conference at Tientsin at which it was decided that, should the necessity arise, the Kwantung Army be dispatched, under some pretext, to take direct part in the fighting in East Suiyuan.

It is generally believed that several Chinese air squadrons have arrived at the front and will soon take part in the operations.

Messrs. Wong Siao Lan(王曉籟), Ling Kong Hou(林康侯) and six other representatives appointed by the various public bodies in Shanghai arrived at Taiyuan by air on November 24, carrying with them a sum of $100,000 contributed by the public in Shanghai. At 5 p.m. they had an interview with General Yen Hsi Shan. They will leave for Suiyuan on November 25.

Sin Wan Pao and other local newspapers :-

Measures to Centralise the Collection of Contributions.

Yesterday Mr. Dong Ying Bah(董行白), member of the Standing Committee of local Kuomintang Headquarters, had a conference with Mayor Wu Te Chen over the question of centralising the collection of contributions in aid of the Government troops in Suiyuan.

The matter will be brought before a meeting of the Executive Committee of the local Tangpu for discussion, after which a meeting of local official organs and public bodies will be convened.

1936年11月25日。上午译文

《大公报》及其他本地报纸刊登如下电报报道：

绥远局势：中国政府军队占领百灵庙。

中国政府军队于11月24日上午9时30分占领百灵庙。

获悉约5000名蒙古及满洲国士兵援军将于11月24日下午抵达百灵庙的情报后，曾延授将军指挥的政府军队于11月24日凌晨1时从武川和固阳对百灵庙发动全面进攻。蒙古及满洲国军队由某国的200名军官指挥。随后爆发激战，政府军于上午9时30分占领百灵庙。政府军伤亡300人，而敌军被歼灭。中国骑兵正在追击逃窜的蒙古及满洲国部队以及某国人员。

由于德王急于向中国政府投降，某国已任命特务机关长田中严密监视德王的行动。

11月24日，驻扎在华北的日军高级军官在天津举行会议，决定如有必要，将以某种借口派遣关东军直接参加绥东战事。

普遍相信，数个中国空军中队已抵达前线，并将很快参与作战。

王晓籁、林康侯等六位由上海各公共团体指派的代表，携带上海民众捐赠的10万元，于11月24日乘飞机抵达太原。下午5时，他们会见了阎锡山将军。他们将于11月25日前往绥远。

《新闻报》及其他本地报纸：

集中募集捐款的措施。

昨日，本地国民党党部常务委员董行白先生与市长吴铁城就集中募集援助绥远政府军队捐款一事举行会谈。

此事将提交本地党部执行委员会会议讨论，之后将召集本地官署和公共团体开会。

上午

1936年11月25日。

《大公报》及其他本地报纸刊登下列电讯报道：

绥远局势：中国政府军队占领百灵庙。

中国政府军队于11月24日上午9时30分占领百灵庙。

鉴于情报显示约500名蒙古及伪满洲国士兵援军将于11月24日下午抵达百灵庙，曾延榿将军指挥的政府军于11月24日凌晨1时从五原和固阳发起对百灵庙的全面进攻。蒙古及伪满洲国部队由某国的200名军官指挥。随后爆发激战，政府军于上午9时30分占领百灵庙。政府军伤亡300人，敌军被全歼。中国骑兵正在追击溃逃的蒙古及伪满洲国部队以及某国人员。

由于德王急于向中国政府投降，某国已任命特务机关长田中密切监视德王的动向。

11月24日，驻扎在华北的日军高级军官在天津举行会议，决定如有必要，将以某种借口派遣关东军直接参与绥东战事。

普遍相信，数个中国空军中队已抵达前线，并将很快参战。

王晓兰、林康侯先生及上海各公共团体推举的其他六名代表，携带上海公众捐赠的10万元款项，于11月24日乘飞机抵达太原。下午5时，他们会见了阎锡山将军。他们将于11月25日前往绥远。

《新闻报》及其他本地报纸：

集中募集捐款的措施。

昨日，当地国民党总部常务委员董行白先生就集中募集援助绥远政府军捐款一事，与市长吴铁城举行会谈。

此事将提交当地党部执行委员会会议讨论，随后将召集当地官方机构和公共团体开会。

November 24, 1936. Morning Translation.

Sin Wan Pao and other local newspapers publish the following telegraphic reports :-

THE FIGHTING IN SUIYUAN

According to information given out by the bandit and "Manchukuo" forces, a general offensive will be launched by them in North Suiyuan on November 27.
According to a telegraphic report received from Changpe, a military leader of a certain nation is at present holding meetings in Jehol and Dolonor to discuss plans for a general offensive in Suiyuan. A large number of fighting planes equipped with inflammable bombs have been mobilized at Dolonor.
During the past few days, large numbers of Jehol and bandit troops have arrived at Dolonor and many military officers of a certain nation are mingling with them.
On November 22, seventeen aeroplanes flew over Shing Woo and dropped 12 bombs on a village, killing 7 persons.

National Herald and other local newspapers :-

Six Local Merchants to Visit Front

On November 23, Mayor Wu Te Chen dispatched the following telegram to General Yen Hsi Shan :-
"The bandits are invading Suiyuan. Our officers and men engaged in the suppression of the bandits are repulsing the attacks and several victories have been won. The 'Committee to Send Consolation and Aid to the Officers and Men engaged in Bandit Suppression in Suiyuan Province' of Shanghai has now appointed Messrs Wong Shiao Lai (王曉), Yen Foh Ching (顏福慶), Huang Jen Ts (黃任之), Ling Kong Hou (林康侯), Loh Ching Sz (陸京士) and another to proceed to-day (November 23) by aeroplane to Shensi whence they will visit the front line in Suiyuan to make an inspection and to console the officers and men. They are leaving to-day (November 23). I hope you will attend to them".
Yesterday the Mayor sent a similar telegram to General Fu Tso Nyi, Chairman of the Suiyuan Provincial Government, informing him of the visit of the representatives to the front line.

Messrs Wong Shiao Lai, Ling Kong Hou, Huang Jen Ts, Loh Ching Sz, Yen Foh Ching, Pang Ching Tseu (龐京周) and Lu Yeu Yuen (陸友元), seven representatives appointed by the "Committee to Send Consolation and Aid to the Officers and Men engaged in Bandit Suppression in Suiyuan Province", left the Hungjao Aerodrome for the North in an aeroplane at 10.15 a.m. yesterday. Mr. Wong Shou Fah (王守法), a son of Mr. Wong Shiao Lai, is also one of the party. Messrs Doo Yuet Sen (杜月笙), Chien Sing Ts (錢新之), Tsu Hsueh Van (朱學範) and many others saw them off.
The representatives will arrive at Sian at 3.30 p.m. November 23 and pass the night there. On the morning of November 24, they will fly to Taiyuan to interview General Yen Hsi Shan, after which they will proceed to Suiyuan where they will call on General Fu Tso Nyi and will console the officers and men at the front and make an inspection. They will return to Shanghai after five days.

1936年11月24日。上午译件。

《新闻报》及其他本地报纸刊登下列电讯报道：

绥远战事

据匪军及“伪满洲国”部队发布的消息，他们将于11月27日在绥北发动全面进攻。
据来自张北的电讯报道，某国的一位军事领袖目前正在热河和多伦诺尔举行会议，讨论在绥远发动全面进攻的计划。多伦诺尔已动员了大量配备燃烧弹的战斗机。
过去几天，大量热河部队和匪军抵达多伦诺尔，许多某国军官混迹其中。
11月22日，十七架飞机飞越兴武，在一个村庄投下12枚炸弹，造成7人死亡。

《国民日报》及其他本地报纸：

六名本地商人将前往前线

11月23日，吴铁城市长向阎锡山将军发出如下电报：
“匪徒进犯绥远。我军剿匪官兵击退进攻，屡获胜利。上海‘慰问援助绥远省剿匪将士委员会’现已指派王晓、颜福庆、黄任之、林康侯、陆京士等先生及另一人，于今日（11月23日）乘飞机前往陕西，随后前往绥远前线视察并慰劳将士。他们于今日（11月23日）启程。望予接待。”
昨日，市长向绥远省政府主席傅作义将军发出类似电报，通报代表们前往前线的情况。

王晓、林康侯、黄任之、陆京士、颜福庆、庞京周和陆友元七位先生，系由“慰问援助绥远省剿匪将士委员会”推举的代表，于昨日上午10时15分从虹桥机场乘飞机北上。王晓之子王守法先生亦随行。杜月笙、钱新之、朱学范等先生及多人前往送行。
代表们将于11月23日下午3时30分抵达西安，并在那里过夜。11月24日上午，他们将飞往太原会见阎锡山将军，随后前往绥远，拜访傅作义将军，慰劳前线将士并进行视察。他们将在五天后返回上海。

November 24, 1936. Morning Translation.

At a weekly memorial service held by the
Shih Chung Middle School for Girls ( 市中女中 ), Nanyang
Road, yesterday morning, Miss Chen Nai Wen ( 陈乃文 ),
the principal, made a report on the movement among the
schools to raise contributions towards the support of
the troops in Suiyuan.
Moved by the report, some 20 students set
out in the afternoon to solicit contributions from the
public. At 5.30 p.m. two girl students were arrested
and taken by foreign policemen to Sinza Station as
they were raising contributions from pedestrians on the
pavement on the east side of the Park Hotel on Bubbling
Well Road.
Upon receipt of this information, Mr. Chang
Chung Yin ( 张仲寅 ), Chairman of the Board of Directors
of the school, immediately called at Sinza Station in
person and opened negotiations, as a result of which the
two girls were released shortly after 6 p.m. It is
reported that a sum of $20 was raised by them yesterday.

With a view to supporting the officers and
men in Suiyuan, some 200 students of the Dah Dong University
( 大同大学 ) held a meeting yesterday at which it was resolved
that contributions be raised from November 23 to December 2;
that the proceeds be used for the purchase of 100 pieces
of fur clothing and 100 steel helmets and gas masks for
the officers and men at the front.

In order to purchase padded cotton vests
and medicines for the defence force in Suiyuan, the Pei
Zung ( 培成 ) Girls School on Ferry Road is endeavouring
to raise by contributions a sum of $5,000. Of this amount,
$4,600 have already been collected.

The following collections are announced:-
1) Teaching staff and coolies of Chaotung University
( 交通大学 ) - $1,700.
2) Employees of the Chinese Telephone Administration of
the Ministry of Communications - $570.
3) Employees of the General Affairs Department of the China
Opel Electric Bulb Factory - $200.
4) Members of the 27th Squad of the 5th Squadron of the
2nd Period Citizenship Training - $150.
5) Teaching staff, students and coolies of the Shanghai
Medical College and the Nurses Training School of its
First Hospital - $1,241.92.

At a meeting held by the Tao Chung ( 通中 )
Middle School for Girls, it was resolved that the teaching
staff contribute 5% of their pay towards the support of the
troops in Suiyuan.

At a meeting held by the Jao Kwang ( 侨光 )
Middle School, the following resolutions were passed:-
1) That the teaching staff contribute one day's pay.
2) That each student contribute at least 30 cents.
3) That teachers and students fast for one day and remit
the money saved to Suiyuan.

1936年11月24日。上午译件。

昨天上午，位于南阳路的市立女子中学举行每周纪念仪式，校长陈乃文女士报告了各校为支援绥远军队而开展的募捐运动情况。
受报告感召，约20名学生于下午出发向公众募捐。下午5时30分，两名女学生在静安寺路国际饭店东侧人行道上向行人募捐时被外籍警察逮捕，并带至新闸捕房。
获悉此情况后，该校董事会董事长张仲寅先生立即亲自前往新闸捕房进行交涉，结果两名女生于下午6时过后不久获释。据报道，她们昨日募得20元。

为支援绥远将士，大同大学约200名学生昨日举行会议，决议从11月23日至12月2日进行募捐；所得款项用于购买100件皮衣以及100顶钢盔和防毒面具，供前线将士使用。

为购买棉背心和药品以支援绥远防卫部队，渡船路上的培成女校正努力通过募捐筹集5,000元。目前已募集到4,600元。

公布以下捐款名单：
1) 交通大学教职员及苦力——1,700元。
2) 交通部中华电话局职员——570元。
3) 中国奥佩尔灯泡厂总务部职员——200元。
4) 第二期公民训练第五队第27小队队员——150元。
5) 上海医学院及其第一医院护士学校教职员、学生及苦力——1,241.92元。

通中女子中学举行会议，决议教职员捐出薪水的5%以支援绥远军队。

侨光中学举行会议，通过以下决议：
1) 教职员捐出一天薪水。
2) 每名学生至少捐款3角。
3) 师生禁食一天，将节省下来的钱汇往绥远。

At 3 p.m. yesterday, the 15th District Branch

meeting at which it was reported that the North Soochow
Road Branch of the National Commercial Bank had received
contributions amounting to $130 from the Woo Suh Iron

At a meeting held by the Union of workers of
the Kiangnan Dock yesterday, it was resolved to contribute

At 10.30 a.m. the other day, students of the

thrift and frugality and save the money for contribution
to Suiyuan.
3) That the teachers and students solicit contributions

The Electrical Apparatus Manufacturers
Association has issued a circular notice to its members
notifying that commencing from this month, they will
contribute one day's income every month to Suiyuan.

Yesterday the Executive and Supervisory
Committees of the Hotel Waiters Union held a meeting, at which
it was resolved to issue a circular notice directing members
to contribute one day's pay.

Dr. H.H. Kung, Minister of Finance, has remitted
a sum of $10,000 to Suiyuan to console the officers and
men at the front.

Mr. Zang Sung Yee (盛昇), Chief of the Consolidated
Tax Bureau of Kiangsu, Chekiang and Anhwei, has collected
from his staff a sum of $10,000 which he has requested
Dr. H.H. Kung to remit to Suiyuan.

The employees of the Shanghai-Nanking and
Shanghai-Hangchow-Ningpo Railway Administration have
made a further contribution of $10,000. The money
was remitted to Suiyuan on November 21 through the Shanghai
Commercial and Savings Bank.

4) 组建30个募捐小组。
这些小组已从公众处募集到200元。

昨日下午3时，第一特区市民联合会第十五区分会举行会议，会上报告称，国家商业银行北苏州路分行收到可铁行等捐赠的130元。

昨日江南码头工人联合会举行会议，决议捐款500元。

日前上午10时30分，滨海中学学生举行会议，通过以下决议：
1) 立即成立“滨海学生支援绥远剿匪部队委员会”。
2) 全体师生厉行节约，将省下的钱捐往绥远。
3) 师生向亲友邻居募捐。

电器制造业同业公会向其会员发出通告，通知自本月起，每月将一天的收入捐往绥远。

昨日，酒楼侍者工会执行委员会和监察委员会举行会议，决议发出通告，指示会员捐出一天薪水。

财政部长孔祥熙博士已汇款10,000元至绥远，以慰劳前线将士。

江苏、浙江、安徽统税局局长盛昇先生从其职员中募集到10,000元，并已请求孔祥熙博士将该款汇往绥远。

京沪及沪杭甬铁路管理局员工再次捐款10,000元。该笔款项已于11月21日通过上海商业储蓄银行汇往绥远。

昨日上午，位于南阳路的市女中（Shih Chung Middle School for Girls）举行每周纪念仪式，校长陈乃文小姐就学校界发起募捐以支援绥远部队的运动作了报告。
受该报告感召，约20名学生于下午出发向社会公众募捐。下午5时30分，两名女学生在静安寺路（Bubbling Well Road）国际饭店东侧人行道上向行人募捐时，被外籍警察逮捕并带至新闸捕房。
获悉此情况后，该校董事会董事长张仲寅先生立即亲自前往新闸捕房进行交涉，结果两名女生于下午6时过后不久获释。据报道，她们昨日共募得20元。

为支援绥远官兵，大同大学（Dah Dong University）约200名学生昨日举行会议，决议从11月23日至12月2日进行募捐；所得款项用于购买100件皮衣以及100顶钢盔和防毒面具，供前线官兵使用。

为购买棉背心和药品以供绥远防卫队使用，斐成女中（Pei Jung Girls School，位于渡船路 Ferry Road）正努力募集5,000元捐款。目前该金额中已筹集4,600元。

公布以下捐款情况：-
1) 交通大学（Chaotung University）教职员及苦力 - 1,700元。
2) 交通部中华电话局职员 - 570元。
3) 中国亚浦耳灯泡厂总务部职员 - 200元。
4) 第二期公民训练第五队第二十七小队队员 - 150元。
5) 上海医学院及其第一医院护士学校之教职员、学生及苦力 - 1,241.92元。

在道中女中（Tao Chung Middle School for Girls）举行的会议上，决议教职员捐出薪水的5%以支援绥远部队。

在侨光中学（Jao Kwang Middle School）举行的会议上，通过以下决议：-
1) 教职员捐出一日薪水。
2) 每名学生至少捐款30分。
3) 师生绝食一日，将省下的钱汇往绥远。

pages.en:
November 24, 1936.    5    Morning Translation.

4) That 30 contribution soliciting groups be formed.
The groups have already collected $200 from
the public.

At 3 p.m. yesterday, the 15th District Branch
of the First Special District Citizens' Federation held a
meeting at which it was reported that the North Soochow
Road Branch of the National Commercial Bank had received
contributions amounting to $130 from the Woo Suh Iron
Hong (可燼铁行) and others.

At a meeting held by the Union of workers of
the Kiangnan Dock yesterday, it was resolved to contribute
$500.

At 10.30 a.m. the other day, students of the
Ping Hai (濱海) Middle School held a meeting at which
the following resolutions were passed:-
1) That a "Ping Hai Students Committee to Support the Bandit
Suppression Force in Suiyuan" be inaugurated immediately.
2) That the entire body of teachers and students practise
thrift and frugality and save the money for contribution
to Suiyuan.
3) That the teachers and students solicit contributions
from their relatives and neighbours.

The Electrical Apparatus Manufacturers
Association has issued a circular notice to its members
notifying that commencing from this month, they will
contribute one day's income every month to Suiyuan.

Yesterday the Executive and Supervisory
Committees of the Hotel Waiters Union held a meeting at which
it was resolved to issue a circular notice directing members
to contribute one day's pay.

Dr. H.H. Kung, Minister of Finance, has remitted
a sum of $10,000 to Suiyuan to console the officers and
men at the front.

Mr. Zang Sung Yee (盛昇頤), Chief of the Consolidated
Tax Bureau of Kiangsu, Chekiang and Anhwei, has collected
from his staff a sum of $10,000 which he has requested
Dr. H.H. Kung to remit to Suiyuan.

The employees of the Shanghai-Nanking and
Shanghai-Hangchow-Ningpo Railway Administration have
made a further contribution of $10,000. The money
was remitted to Suiyuan on November 21 through the Shanghai
Commercial and Savings Bank.
pages.zh:
1936年11月24日。    5    晨间译件。

4) 组建30个募捐小组。
各小组已从公众处募集到200元。

昨日下午3时，第一特区市民联合会第十五区分会举行会议，会上报告称，国家银行北苏州路分行收到可燼铁行（Woo Suh Iron Hong）等方的捐款共计130元。

在昨日江南码头工人工会举行的会议上，决议捐款500元。

前日上午10时30分，滨海中学（Ping Hai Middle School）学生举行会议，通过以下决议：-
1) 立即成立“滨海学生支援绥远剿匪部队委员会”。
2) 全体师生厉行节约，将省下的钱捐献给绥远。
3) 师生向亲友邻居募捐。

电器制造同业公会向其会员发出通告，通知自本月起，每月捐献一日收入给绥远。

昨日，酒楼侍者工会执行委员会和监察委员会举行会议，决议发出通告，指示会员捐出一日薪水。

财政部长孔祥熙博士已向绥远汇款10,000元，以慰劳前线官兵。

江苏、浙江、安徽统税局局长盛昇頤（Zang Sung Yee）先生从其职员处募集了10,000元，并请孔祥熙博士汇往绥远。

京沪、沪杭甬铁路管理局职员再次捐款10,000元。该笔款项已于11月21日通过上海商业储蓄银行汇往绥远。

pages.en:
2.
November 23, 1936. Morning Translation.

Foreign Affairs for a further parley with General Chang Chun
on the afternoon of November 23. Up to a late hour last
night, no information was given out by the Ministry of Foreign
Affairs and it is not known whether General Chang Chun will
meet the Japanese Ambassador on the afternoon of November 23.
The object of the invasion of Suiyuan by the
bandit and the "Manchukuo" forces under the protection of
a certain nation and where Japanese aeroplanes and field
guns are playing an active part is clear. The public
bodies in Nanking are of opinion that negotiations under
such circumstances would prove useless.

At 10.30 a.m. November 20, seventeen aeroplanes
belonging to the bandit forces flew over the regions
north-east of Hsin Hu. Several bombs were dropped; seven
persons were killed and many houses were destroyed.

Prince Tuh will soon define his attitude towards
the operations in Suiyuan. He will not take part in these
activities. He has suddenly left for Sien Su Nyi with
more than 300 of his soldiers.
According to a telegram from Tientsin, Princes
Tuh and Tso have already issued telegrams formally announcing
their participation in the movement of the bandit and puppet
forces. They have assumed the titles of Commander-in-Chief
and Vice Commander-in-Chief respectively of the forces for
the development of Mongolia and for the suppression of
communists.

Ta Kung Pao, Shun Pao and other local newspapers:

Activities of Local Public Bodies

Yesterday the Shanghai Municipality Chinese
Theatrical Players' Society held at its office a general
meeting of representatives of its various subsidiary organs
to discuss the question of rendering assistance to the officers
and men defending Suiyuan Province. About 40 persons were
present. Mr. Ting Siu Daung (丁守棠) presided.
The following resolutions were passed:-
1) That a committee be organized by the Chinese Theatrical
Players' Society to support the Suiyuan officers and men
who are resisting the enemy; that the public be invited to join
the committee.
2) That an open letter addressed to local theatrical players
be issued soliciting subscriptions in aid of the troops
in Suiyuan.
3) That a move ment to collect subscriptions from theatrical
players be commenced from date.
4) That the entire body of theatrical players propagate,
during performances or while broadcasting, the resistance
that is being put up by the defence force in Suiyuan so
that the attention of the people may be drawn to the work
of national salvation and be induced to contribute towards
the support of the troops in Suiyuan.
pages.zh:
2.
1936年11月23日。晨间译件。

外交部将于11月23日下午与张群将军进一步商谈。直至昨晚深夜，外交部未发布任何消息，尚不清楚张群将军是否会在11月23日下午会见日本大使。
在某国庇护下，且有日本飞机和野战炮积极参与的情况下，匪军及“满洲国”军队进犯绥远的目的显而易见。南京各界团体认为，在此种情况下进行谈判将是徒劳的。

11月20日上午10时30分，十七架属于匪军的飞机飞越新湖（Hsin Hu）东北地区。投下数枚炸弹；七人死亡，许多房屋被毁。

德王（Prince Tuh）即将表明其对绥远作战的态度。他不会参与这些活动。他突然率领300多名士兵前往西苏尼特（Sien Su Nyi）。
据天津电报称，德王和卓王（Prince Tso）已发出通电，正式宣布参加匪伪军队的运动。他们分别担任蒙古军政府及剿共军总司令和副总司令职务。

《大公报》、《申报》及其他本地报纸：-

本地公共团体的活动

昨日，上海市中国戏剧演员联谊社在其办事处召开各下属机构代表大会，讨论援助保卫绥远省官兵事宜。约40人出席。丁守棠（Ting Siu Daung）先生主持。
通过以下决议：-
1) 由中国戏剧演员联谊社组织一个委员会，以支援抵抗敌人的绥远官兵；邀请公众加入该委员会。
2) 向本地戏剧演员发出一封公开信，募集捐款以援助绥远部队。
3) 即日起开始向戏剧演员募捐的运动。
4) 全体戏剧演员在演出或广播期间，宣传绥远防卫队的抵抗行动，以引起民众对救国工作的关注，并诱导其捐款支援绥远部队。

3.
November 23, 1936. Morning Translation.

5) That a date be fixed for the broadcasting of a special
programme for the purpose of raising subscriptions from
the general public.
Yesterday the Suiyuan Support Committee which was
formed on the night of November 17 by Mr. Tuan Moh Yen
(端木楨) and other inhabitants of the Village for Poor People
on Da.. Moh Jao Road (大木橋路) held an extensive propaganda
meeting in the village. About 1,000 persons were present.
Mr. Zao Zai Sung (肇瑞生) presided.
A man named Shu Wen (舒文) delivered a speech
urging his hearers to save the country from the present crisis.
One Miss Loh Mo Zao (駱慕曹) spoke of the cruelty
that is being endured by the people living in territories
that have been lost to China.
A man named Lee Tuh Yoong (李德榮) pointed out
that only the enforcement of the New Life Movement could
bring about the consolidation of the foundations of the
country.
At the close of the meeting, four kinds of
propaganda dealing with the following matters were distributed:
1) How to save Suiyuan and the country (Continental Policy
and Ocean Policy),
2) A sketch of the Suiyuan front,
3) A general map showing the territory that has been lost
to China during the past 30 years
4) General information about Suiyuan.

Yesterday a movement to raise subscriptions in
the village was started. Several persons named Messrs.
Zing Chi Ling (陳紀麟), Tseu Sing Jen (周信仁), Tuan Moh
Yen and Koh Ngoh Zai (郭玉才) were appointed to solicit
subscriptions from relatives and friends outside the village.

At 6 p.m. yesterday representatives of 44 local
trade associations, including the Shanghai Salt Fish Trade
Association, the Flower Dealers Association, the Ham Dealers
Association, etc, attended a dinner party at the Tsu Mei Lau
Restaurant (致美樓), Foochow Road. Mr. Ching Tsoo Siang
(金祖湘) presided.
The following resolutions were passed:-
1) That each trade association contribute one day's income
towards the support of the Suiyuan troops.
2) That a telegram pledging their full support to the troops
defending Suiyuan be sent.

The 15th Branch Office of the Shanghai First
Special District Citizens' Federation has adopted the following
measures to handle subscriptions from shops on South and
North Soochow Roads:-
1) That the North Soochow Road Branch of the National Commercial
Bank be appointed to receive all subscriptions.
2) That no Branch of the Federation be allowed to receive
donations; that no Branch be allowed to appoint any of its
officials to collect subscriptions from the public.
3) That Mr. Tsoh Ts Zung (祝彥純) be appointed in charge of
propaganda work; that Mr. Ling Mei Ching (林曼卿),
Manager of the North Soochow Road Branch of the National
Commercial Bank, be appointed as custodian of subscriptions.

3.
1936年11月23日。晨间译件。

5) 确定一个日期，广播特别节目，旨在向公众募集捐款。
昨日，由大木桥路贫民窟居民端木楨先生等人于11月17日晚成立的绥远后援会，在该贫民窟举行了一次大型宣传集会。约有1,000人出席。肇瑞生先生主持会议。
一位名叫舒文的男子发表演讲，呼吁听众拯救国家于当前危机之中。
一位名叫駱慕曹的女士讲述了在中国失地生活的人民所遭受的残酷待遇。
一位名叫李德榮的男子指出，只有实行新生活运动，才能巩固国家基础。
会议结束时，分发了四种涉及以下事项的宣传品：
1) 如何拯救绥远及国家（大陆政策与海洋政策），
2) 绥远前线概况，
3) 过去30年间中国丧失领土的总地图，
4) 关于绥远的一般信息。

昨日，该贫民窟开始了募捐活动。指定陈纪麟、周信仁、端木楨和郭玉才等几位先生向村外的亲友募集捐款。

昨日下午6时，包括上海咸鱼业同业公会、花商业同业公会、火腿业同业公会等在内的44个本地同业公会的代表，参加了在福州路致美樓餐馆举行的晚宴。金祖湘先生主持会议。
通过了以下决议：-
1) 各同业公会捐献一日收入，以支援绥远军队。
2) 发送电报，承诺全力支持保卫绥远的军队。

上海第一特区市民联合会第十五办事处已采取以下措施，处理苏州路南段和北段商铺的捐款事宜：-
1) 指定国家商业银行苏州路北段分行接收所有捐款。
2) 不允许联合会任何分会接收捐赠；不允许任何分会指派其官员向公众募集捐款。
3) 指定祝彥純先生负责宣传工作；指定国家商业银行苏州路北段分行经理林曼卿先生为捐款保管人。

4
November 23, 1936. Morning Translation.

The "Committee to Send Consolation and Aid to the Officers and Men engaged in Bandit Suppression in Suiyuan Province", organized by the Chinese Chamber of Commerce, the Shanghai District Association and the Chinese Red Cross Association, has decided to collect contributions and articles to be sent to the officers and men at the front in Suiyuan.

On November 18, Mr. Doo Yuet Sen remitted $100,000 to Suiyuan. He had at first planned to proceed to Suiyuan in company with Mr. Wong Shiao Lai, Chairman of the Chamber of Commerce, but owing to pressing business engagements he has abandoned the proposed visit.

On November 22, the Committee resolved to detail five representatives to Suiyuan. The following gentlemen have been named to make the visit: Messrs Ling Kong Hou (林康侯), Huang Jen Ts (黄任之), Pang Ching Tseu (庞京周), Loh Ching Sz (陆京士) and Wong Shiao Lai. They will leave Shanghai on the morning of November 23 by aeroplane. Mr. Ling says that they will first stop at Sian, whence they will proceed to Taiyuan and Suiyuan. They expect to return to Shanghai in about five days.

With the object of persuading women throughout the country to render assistance to the officers and men at the front in Suiyuan, some 30 representatives of local Chinese women's bodies including Miss Sz Liang (史良) and Miss Chen Foo Eur (陈波儿) held a meeting the other day, at which it was resolved to form a Preparatory Committee of "Chinese Women's Association to Support the Officers and Men at the Front in Suiyuan". Miss Hu Ts Yin (胡子婴) and Miss Beh Vee (白薇) and several others were appointed to undertake the formation of the Association and to induce other women's bodies or individual women to join the association.

Owing to the cold weather in Suiyuan, the Students Native Products Development Movement Group has promoted the raising of contributions in order to buy cotton clothing to be sent to the front.

On the morning of November 22, the students formed into some 20 parties to solicit contributions on Nanking Road and vicinity from the owners of large shops and from customers. They withdrew at noon. The money raised is being kept by the Shanghai Native Goods Movement Federation.

On November 21, the teachers and students of Aurora University remitted to General Fu Tso Nyi of Suiyuan a sum of $1,000 collected from among themselves.

The New China Medical College (新中國醫院), Wongkeshaw, has collected from its teachers and students a sum of some $200. Mr. Tsu Nan San (朱南山), President, and Dr. Tsu Ngau Kao (朱鹤皋), Vice President of the College, suggested that all Chinese doctors be asked to contribute one-day's income towards the fund in aid of the officers and men at the front.

1936年11月23日。晨间译件。

由中华总商会、上海特别市党部和中国红十字会组织的“慰劳绥远剿匪将士委员会”，决定募集捐款和物品，送往绥远前线的将士。

11月18日，杜月笙先生汇往绥远10万元。他原计划与商会主席王晓籁先生一同前往绥远，但因公务繁忙，取消了此次行程。

11月22日，该委员会决议派遣五名代表前往绥远。被指名前往访问的绅士有：林康侯、黄任之、庞京周、陆京士和王晓籁诸先生。他们将于11月23日上午乘飞机离开上海。林先生说，他们将先停在西安，然后前往太原和绥远。预计约五天后返回上海。

为了说服全国妇女援助绥远前线将士，包括史良女士和陈波儿女士在内的约30名本地中国妇女团体代表日前举行会议，决议成立“中国妇女慰劳绥远前线将士协会筹备委员会”。指定胡子婴女士、白薇女士及其他几人负责组建该协会，并劝诱其他妇女团体或个人加入该协会。

由于绥远天气寒冷，学生国货运动促进会推动募捐，以便购买棉衣送往前线。

11月22日上午，学生们组成约20个小组，在南京路及周边地区向大商店店主和顾客募捐。中午时分散去。所募款项正由上海国货运动联合会保管。

11月21日，震旦大学的师生将自行募集的1,000元汇款给绥远傅作义将军。

虹口的新中國醫院从师生中募集了约200元。该院院长朱南山先生和副院长朱鹤皋博士建议，请所有中国医生捐献一日收入，作为援助前线将士的基金。

5
November 23, 1936. Morning Translation.

The teachers and students of t Sz Chen
Middle School (斯威中学), Tou Kia Road, Nantao, have
contributed a sum of $132.32 and sent it to the Bank of
China for remittance to Suiyuan.

More than 30 magazine publishers, including
the Eastern Miscellany, have issued a manifesto urging
readers throughout the country to contribute one-day's
income towards the fund in aid of the officers and men at
the front in Suiyuan. Contributions may be sent to the
Livelihood Weekly (生活周刊社), No. 160 Avenue Edward VII,
the World Knowledge (世界知识社), No. 384 Foochow Road,
the Yen Sz Kia (现世杂志社) in the Chung Wei Bank Building,
Avenue Edward VII, and the Intelligence (读书生活社), Love
Lane, Bubbling Well Road.

The Liang Tsai Women's Supplementary School
(量才女补习学校) has formed a "Committee to Collect
Contributions in aid of Suiyuan". The students will
solicit contributions from relatives and friends.

On November 21, Mr. Koo Nan Jin (顾南群),
President of the Nanyang Hospital (南洋医院), Small East
Gate, Nantao, held an urgent meeting with his employees
to discuss the raising of contributions. A sum of
$135.50 was collected.

The Wha Shing Tobacco Factory (华成烟厂),
Wayside Road, is arranging to collect contributions from
its directors and workers. The matter is being handled
together with the 4th District Rolled Tobacco Trade Labour
Union.

Mr. Lu Tseng (罗飞), Manager of the Dah Chung
(大中) Cleaning & Dyeing Works, No. 18 North Szechuen
Road, has decided to contribute 10 per cent of his takings
from November 23 to November 29 towards the fund for the
officers and men at the front in Suiyuan.

Local Tangpu to Hold Meeting To-day to Discuss the Collection
of Contributions.

The local Tangpu and other organizations the
other day held a meeting and decided to form a Central
Subscriptions Collecting Committee to take charge of
contributions. Soliciting of contributions on the
streets will be strictly prohibited unless permission
has been secured beforehand from the authorities.
The Tangpu will exchange views with the
Shanghai City Government to-day regarding the formation
of a Committee to be known as "The Central Patriotic
Contributions Collecting Committee".

5
1936年11月23日。晨间译件。

南市窦家路的斯威中学师生捐款132.32元，并已送至中国银行，以便汇往绥远。

包括《东方杂志》在内的30多家杂志出版商发表宣言，呼吁全国读者捐献一日收入，作为援助绥远前线将士的基金。捐款可寄至爱多亚路160号《生活周刊社》、福州路384号《世界知识社》、爱多亚路中伟银行大楼内的《现世杂志社》，以及静安寺路爱文义路口的《读书生活社》。

量才女补习学校成立了“募集援绥捐款委员会”。学生将向亲友募捐。

11月21日，南市小东门的南洋医院院长顾南群先生与员工召开紧急会议，讨论募集捐款事宜。共募集到135.50元。

华德路的华成烟厂正在安排向其董事和工人募集捐款。此事正与第四区卷烟业工会共同处理。

四川北路18号大中洗染行经理罗飞先生决定，将其11月23日至11月29日的营业额的10%捐献给绥远前线将士基金。

本地塘浦今日将举行会议讨论募集捐款事宜。

At 10 a.m. yesterday, the Chinese Seamen's Tangpu and the Seamen's Union held a meeting at the latter's office to discuss the question of sending consolation to the Suiyuan troops. Mr. Wong Chi Ih (王峙一) presided.
The following resolutions were passed:-
1) That a Committee of Chinese Seamen to Console the Troops in Suiyuan be formed.
2) That 43 persons, including Messrs. Bang Pah Wei (彭伯威), Wong Tsang Kaung (王仲剛) and Hu Gee (胡琦) be appointed to serve on the Committee.

The Committee yesterday issued circular notices to the various local trade associations requesting them to raise subscriptions.
The Committee has sent a letter to the International Dispensary expressing its appreciation for its contribution of $2,000.

Yesterday the Customs Chinese Staff Club remitted $10,000 to General Fu Tso Nyi, Chairman of the Suiyuan Provincial Government.

Yesterday Mr. Wu Wen Tsoo (吳溫初), Manager of the Tien Lee Nitrogen Factory, remitted $1,000 to General Fu Tso Nyi.

November 22, 1936. Morning Translation

Sin Wan #ao and other local newspapers publish the following
telegraphic reports:-

SITUATION IN SUIYUAN.

After having been badly defeated, the Manchukuo
and Mongolian irregulars under the command of Li Shou Sin
and Wong Ying have decided to abandon their plan of
invading South Suiyuan and will, it is reported, attack
North Suiyuan. In all these irregulars number 25,000
officers and men, in addition instructors of a certain
nation are attached to every company.
On November 21 several tens of officers and
soldiers of the Government forces were either killed or
wounded and 17 motor cars were destroyed by bombs dropped
by aeroplanes of the enemy forces. At the same time
one of these aeroplanes was destroyed by the Government
forces.
It is reported that reinforcements numbering
some 20,000 men stationed at Mukden will be transferred
to the front.

Activities of Local Public Bodies.

Mr. Doo Yuet Sen has sent a telegram to General Yen
Hsi Shan, informing him that apart from remitting a sum of
$100,000 as an encouragement to the officers and men
engaged in bandit suppression on the Suiyuan front, he
and Mr. Wong Shiao Lai will in the near future go to Shansi
with the object of consoling the men at the front.

With a view to enforcing the one-day's income
movement among the general public, the local Tangpu held
a meeting at 2 p.m. yesterday. Amongst those present were
Mr. Hu Fong Ziang (胡凤翔) of the Shanghai First Special
District Citizens' Federation, Mr. Yih Ziang Kao (叶翔皋)
of the General Labour Union, Mr. Nyien Ngau Sung (严牛声)
of the Chinese Chamber of Commerce, Mr. Tsu Yao Kwen (褚耀坤)
of the Shanghai District Association, Mr. Chuing Zing Yei
(程静宜) of the Shanghai Second Special District Citizens'
Federation and Mr. Li Dah Chao (李大) of the Shanghai
City Government. Mr. Dong Yuin Bah (董行白) of the Tangpu
presided.
The following resolutions were passed :-
1) That a Committee to be known as "The Committee to
Further the One-Day's Income Movement to be donated by
Shanghai Chinese Citizens" be formed.
2) That the Tangpu, the Shanghai City Government, the
Chamber of Commerce, the Shanghai District Association
and the Social Bureau be appointed to be standing members
of the new Committee.
3) That the regular meetings of the new Committee be held
on the 1st and the 15th of every month.
4) That the office of the Committee be temporarily located
in the China Cultural Reconstruction Association,
French Concession.
5) That all local public bodies be requested to instruct
their members to send their one-day's income to the
collecting agencies.

《新闻报》及其他本地报纸刊登下列电讯报道：-

绥远局势。

李守辛（音译）和王英（音译）指挥的伪满洲国及蒙古伪军在遭受重创后，已决定放弃入侵绥南的计划，据报将转而进攻绥北。这些伪军共计官兵25,000人，此外每个连队还配有某国教官。
11月21日，政府军数十名官兵伤亡，敌军飞机投掷炸弹炸毁汽车17辆。与此同时，政府军击落敌机一架。
据报，驻沈阳（Mukden）的约20,000名援军将被调往前线。

本地公共团体的活动。

杜月笙先生致电阎锡山将军，告知除汇去10万元以慰劳在绥远前线剿匪的官兵外，他与王晓籁先生将于近期前往山西，旨在慰问前线将士。

为在公众中推行“一日捐”运动，本地党部于昨日下午2时举行会议。出席者包括上海第一特区市民联合会的胡凤翔先生、总工会的叶翔皋先生、中华总商会的严牛声（音译）先生、上海特别市党部的褚耀坤先生、上海第二特区市民联合会的程静宜（音译）先生以及上海市政府的李大超（音译）先生。会议由党部的董允白（音译）先生主持。
通过以下决议：-
1) 成立名为“上海中国公民一日捐运动促进委员会”的委员会。
2) 指定党部、上海市政府、商会、上海特别市党部和社会局为新委员会的常务委员。
3) 新委员会的例会定于每月1日和15日举行。
4) 委员会办事处暂设于法租界的中国文化重建协会。
5) 请所有本地公共团体指示其成员将一日所得收入送至收款机构。

November 22, 1936. Morning Translation.

The "Association of Chinese Women in Shanghai
to Console the Officers and Men Engaged in Bandit
Suppression in Suiyuan Province" held its first meeting at
6 p.m. yesterday at its office, Rue Boppe, French Concession
and passed the following resolutions :-
1) That Chinese families be persuaded to save ten cents
per day and to collect the money thus obtained in order
that it may be sent to the officers and men at the front
in Suiyuan.
2) That broadcasting stations be requested to conduct
propaganda in favour of the 10-cent per day movement.
3) That deputies be detailed to conduct propaganda among
female workers in factories and mills; that deputies
be detailed to amusement resorts to conduct similar
propaganda.

On November 21, the Chinese Native Products
Maintenance Association held a dinner party in the Kwan
Sun Yuen Restaurant (冠生園), Nanking Road, during which
Mr. Wong Han Jang (王漢章) suggested that contributions
be collected and sent to officers and men engaged in the
suppression of bandits in Suiyuan. It was decided to
hold an urgent meeting next Friday in order to discuss
the subject.

At 3 p.m. yesterday, the students of the
Bah Min (培明) Middle School for Girls on Hart Road formed
20 groups and proceeded to Avenue Haig, Yu Yuen Road,
Bubbling Well Road, Yates Road, Sinza Road, Nanking Road,
and boarded trams in order to solicit contributions towards
a fund in aid of officers and men in Suiyuan. Within two
hours, a sum of some $210 was collected. The girl students
will continue the soliciting campaign.

The students of Aurora University held a
meeting yesterday and passed the following resolutions :-
1) That contributions be solicited from the public.
2) That theatrical performances be given in order to
raise contributions.

Local Chinese cereal bodies and outport
dealers residing in Shanghai held a meeting on November 21
and established a Committee to render assistance to Suiyuan.
A contribution movement will be carried out among the
dealers in a few days.

The China Industrial Federation held a meeting
at its office, Hankow Road, on November 21, at which it
was resolved to send a telegram to General Chiang Kai Shek
requesting him to send reinforcement to the north to aid
in the suppression of bandits in Suiyuan.

“上海中国妇女慰劳绥远剿匪将士协会”于昨晚6时在该会办事处（法租界蒲柏路）举行首次会议，并通过以下决议：-

11月21日，国货维持会在南京路冠生园餐馆举行晚宴，期间王汉章先生建议募集捐款并汇往绥远剿匪将士。决定于下周五召开紧急会议讨论此事。

昨日下午3时，哈特路培明女中的学生组成20个小组，前往海格路、愚园路、静安寺路、耶茨路（音译）、新闸路、南京路，并登上电车，为援助绥远将士基金募捐。在两小时内，共募得约210元。女学生们将继续开展募捐活动。

震旦大学学生昨日举行会议，并通过以下决议：-
1) 向公众募捐。
2) 举行戏剧演出以筹集捐款。

居沪的本地粮食业同业公会及外地客商于11月21日举行会议，成立援助绥远委员会。数日内将在客商中开展募捐运动。

中华工业联合会于11月21日在其汉口路办事处举行会议，决议致电蒋介石将军，请求其派兵北上，协助绥远剿匪。

The General Labour Union, at a meeting held

a) To send representatives to conduct propaganda

b) To distribute brochures on the subject."

The Students Native Products Development
Movement Group has decided to raise contributions from
various shops along Nanking Road on November 22 (Sunday).

Ta Kung Pao and other local newspapers :-

Local dance halls and dance girls have promised
to donate funds in aid of Suiyuan. The employees of the
Metropole and National Ball Rooms contributed $75 which
was sent to the "Ta Kung Pao" on November 21 for remittance
to Suiyuan.
The Chinese employees of the Cathay Hotel, the
Bund, have promoted a one-day movement. On November 21,
they sent all donations to the "Ta Kung Pao". Donations
were also made by two foreigners.

China Times (comment) dated Nov. 21 :-

What Should Be Our Attitude Towards the Suiyuan Invaders?

While the 8th session in the negotiations
between General Chang Chun and Mr. Kawagoe are going on,
Suiyuan is being invaded. Peace in the Far East is thus
threatened.
We have often heard it said, "The Chinese are
insincere in the negotiations." The Japanese recently
declared that should China insist on her views, they would
take action in North China. Now, at this moment when the
negotiations are still going on, the Japanese have taken
action in North China. Of what use are the negotiations?
Japanese claim that the fighting in East Suiyuan
is purely a Chinese question, but the shells and bombs that
are being used by the invaders are "made in Japan." As to
the participation of Japanese in the invasion, Japan is
saying that individual participation by Japanese has nothing
to do with the Japanese Government. However, we submit
for consideration the following two points:-
1) The Japanese Kwantung Army has denied any previous
knowledge of the invasion by the Mongolian invaders, but
it has shown its sympathy towards the invasion. This
Army's open support of the Chinese insurgents is contrary
to international law.
2) The Mongolian and Manchukuo forces are using North Charhar
and Manchukuo as bases of operations. This is due to
the illegal stationing of Japanese troops in these so-
called "special areas." Thus it is established that
the existence of special areas in China is a menace to
the peace and safety of China. For the sake of peace
in China and the Far East, we should make every effort
to remove these so-called special areas.
The attitude of the Kwantung Army is unfriendly
to China; it is suspected of assisting in the civil
disturbances in China. So long as the puppet State of
Manchukuo and the special area of North Charhar remain in
existence, Suiyuan Province cannot be safe.
We should protest against the stationing of
unfriendly foreign troops in Chinese territory; we should
remove all puppet organization and special areas.

总工会在昨日举行的会议上通过以下决议：-

学生国货促进会决定于11月22日（星期日）在南京路各商店募集捐款。

本地舞厅及舞女承诺捐款援助绥远。大都会舞厅和大华舞厅的职员捐款75元，已于11月21日送交《大公报》，以便汇往绥远。
外滩华懋饭店的中国职员发起了一日捐运动。11月21日，他们将所有捐款送交《大公报》。另有两名外籍人士也进行了捐赠。

《时事新报》评论（11月21日刊）：-

我们应对绥远入侵者持何种态度？

在张群将军与川越茂先生的第八轮谈判正在进行之际，绥远正遭到入侵。远东和平因此受到威胁。
我们常听到一种说法：“中国在谈判中缺乏诚意。”日本方面近日宣称，若中国坚持其立场，他们将在华北采取行动。如今，在谈判仍在进行之时，日本已在华北采取行动。谈判又有何用？
日本声称绥东战事纯属中国内部问题，但入侵者使用的炮弹和炸弹却是“日本制造”。至于日本人参与入侵一事，日本称个别日本人的参与与日本政府无关。然而，我们提出以下两点供考量：-
1) 日本关东军否认事先知晓蒙古伪军的入侵，但却对入侵表示同情。该军队公开支持中国叛乱分子，这违反国际法。
2) 蒙古及伪满洲国军队以察哈尔北部和伪满洲国为作战基地。这是由于日军非法驻扎在这些所谓的“特殊区域”所致。因此可以确定，中国境内特殊区域的存在是对中国和平与安全的威胁。为了中国和远东的和平，我们应尽力消除这些所谓的特殊区域。
关东军的态度对中国不友好；涉嫌协助中国的内乱。只要伪满洲国和察哈尔北部特殊区域依然存在，绥远省就无法安全。
我们应抗议不友好的外国军队驻扎在中国领土上；我们应废除所有傀儡组织和特殊区域。
